# RL Training and Exploration

[Home](../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../README.md) · [简体中文](rl-training-exploration_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Common Methods → RL Training and Exploration

Reusable RL training mechanisms and workflow automation, including curriculum learning, task/reset sampling, exploration allocation and Agent-driven training development. Record training changes, configuration sources, policy optimizers, evaluated embodiments and deployment policies. Distinguish training-time Agents from runtime control architectures; sampling existing resets does not generate new configurations.

| [AM.MAN.METHOD.RL.1] <a id="am-man-method-rl-1"></a> | **SGS｜RL · Success-guided sampling · Training-reset scheduling**<br>[A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.12465v1)<br>Octi Zhang, Mateo Guaman Castro, Patrick Yin, Ignacio Dagnino, Abhishek Gupta, Rosario Scalise, Byron Boots<br>**Tags:** `manipulation` `gripper` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `success-guided-sampling` `adaptive-curriculum` `reset-distribution` `training-start-scheduling` `massively-parallel-simulation` `contact-rich-assembly` `quadruped-locomotion` `teacher-student-distillation` `dagger` `rgb-policy` `sim-to-real` | SGS uses recent success rates for task configurations to prioritize training resets that are neither mastered nor currently out of reach, directing more parallel PPO experience toward learnable configurations and improving large-scale robot RL efficiency and capabilities.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A Beta-shaped weight over recent success rates samples a fixed configuration pool, retaining nonzero probability for easy/hard cases. Configurations specify initial state, goal and environment; manipulation resets cover reaching, stable grasp and near-goal starts, with coverage supplied externally. SGS only schedules training; PPO learns actions. Simulation covers 13 quadruped terrain types, six UR5e + Robotiq 2F-85 assembly tasks and Franka parallel-gripper nut-and-bolt assembly. Locomotion uses one multi-terrain policy; manipulation trains per task. At one million environments, Franka nut-and-bolt success is about 70% versus 6% for uniform sampling; simpler tasks benefit less at sufficient scale. DAgger distills UR5e point-cloud teachers into dual-view RGB/proprioceptive students that issue closed-loop end-effector translation/rotation increments and gripper commands on hardware without real-data fine-tuning: nut-and-bolt 18/48, rod insertion 30/49, gear mesh 47/50. This is neither multi-finger-hand validation nor a shared cross-platform policy. Code remains marked coming soon at verification. | CoRL 2026 / arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.12465v1) · [Project](https://sgs-rl.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.METHOD.RL.2] <a id="am-man-method-rl-2"></a> | **HARBOR｜Agent-automated RL training · Staged validation and repair · Parallel tuning and experience reuse**<br>[HARBOR: A Harness Framework for Agentic Robot Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08610v1)<br>Zechu Li, Yufeng Jin, Xiaoyang Liu, Puze Liu, Vignesh Prasad, Carlo D’Eramo, Georgia Chalvatzaki<br>**Tags:** `agent` `training-time-agent` `agentic-rl` `harness-engineering` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `llm-reward-design` `executable-gates` `parallel-tuning` `experience-reuse` `domain-randomization` [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `sac` `td3` `cross-embodiment` `gripper` `dexterous` `bimanual` `locomotion` `sim-to-real` | HARBOR coordinates specialized Agents for task construction, reward design and RL training/tuning, using executable checks for repairs, parallel trials and reusable experience to produce runnable training projects and robot policies.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Simulator code and task specifications enter a staged workflow with persistent artifacts, repair feedback and human intervention after exhausted retries. Experience is external memory, not LLM weight updates. Agents develop training; PPO/SAC/TD3 learn actions, with no online Agent at deployment. Evaluation covers six simulation benchmarks and sixteen tasks spanning manipulation, locomotion and bimanual dexterity. Hardware uses dual Frankas with parallel grippers and xArm UF850 with Allegro V4; 20 Hz policies output end-effector pose or joint-position increments. Platforms train separately. Real-robot interfaces, trajectories and feedback still require humans. Public code, data and checkpoint downloads remain unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08610v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
